interpretation: Valid descriptive motivation for a separately controlled gamma/beta adaptation experiment while keeping moving moments and inference-mode backbone fixed. BN inference is an affine per-channel mapping; gamma/beta can change that mapping without recalibrating moments. This audit does not establish that those parameters are the bottleneck or predict any accuracy gain.
limitations: 36 cached positives are only 3 manifest-order quantile samples per family, with repeated source photos and possible overlapping contexts; this is not random or source-independent population estimation.
Moments pool all spatial positions, including paper/background/verso/unknown regions. They do not isolate foreground Braille activations, and no negatives or stochastic augmentation are sampled.
Mean-shift and std ratios use sqrt(saved_variance+epsilon), not unadjusted stored standard deviation, and are channel medians. ReLU6 saturation is a pooled element fraction.

The report retains observed means/variances, not raw activations or their sums. This review checks the accumulation formula, shapes, stored moments and derived arithmetic; it does not independently reproduce deep-layer moments without inference.

The script checks both all model weight bytes before/after and checkpoint file hash, with gradients disabled and no optimizer/save. Its in-memory before/after equality is evidence from the original run; this review separately verifies the retained checkpoint and its BN moments.

Gamma/beta-only training requires an explicit trainable-variable set and training=False for the nested backbone; merely unfreezing BN under training=True would update moments and test a different hypothesis.
